> **This guide is specific to the Ontario Public Service (OPS).** sharepointless
> itself works in any Microsoft 365 organization. Elsewhere the overall shape is
> the same (register an app, get its permissions approved, sign in from R), but
> the ticket process, and which permissions your IT department will approve,
> will differ. If you're outside the OPS, use this as a map of what to ask your
> IT department for.

## Who needs this

Anyone who wants to use sharepointless (or Microsoft365R directly) and hasn't
yet set up an app registration. **The main obstacle is permissions, not R.**
Your app needs Microsoft Graph permissions that only IT can approve. Once
they're approved, the R side takes a few minutes.

## Overview

This guide gets an OPS user from nothing to reading and writing SharePoint
document libraries from R, signed in as themselves. Following these steps
should take under an hour of your own time, plus however long IT takes to
approve permissions.

The approach: register your own app in Microsoft Entra, have IT approve its
Microsoft Graph permissions, then sign in from R with the **AzureGraph** and
**Microsoft365R** packages. Every call runs as you, so R can never reach
anything you can't already open in the browser.

You need:

- An OPS Microsoft 365 account with access to the SharePoint site you want to
  work with
- R and RStudio on your Windows machine
- Access to the Entra admin centre / Azure portal (App registrations), which
  OPS users had in our case
- Patience with Microsoft's error codes. Every one we hit is in the
  Troubleshooting section.

## Step 1: Register the app in Entra

Useful links: [App registrations in the Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/ActiveDirectoryMenuBlade/~/RegisteredApps)
· the OPS intranet guide *How to Register an App in Microsoft Entra ID* (search
the SharePoint Online portal on the OPS intranet).

1. Sign in to the Azure portal with your OPS account and go to
   **Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations → New registration**.
2. **Name:** anything recognizable. Ours is `Microsoft365R`.
3. **Supported account types:** *Accounts in this organizational directory
   only* (Government of Ontario only, single tenant).
4. Leave the redirect URI blank for now (Step 3 sets it) and click
   **Register**.
5. On the app's **Overview** page, note two values. You'll need both in R:
    - **Application (client) ID**
    - **Directory (tenant) ID**

You become an owner of the registration automatically, which means you can fix
its Authentication settings yourself later without a ticket.

## Step 2: Request API permissions

Request all five permissions below. They look partly redundant, but requests
with fewer haven't worked.

**2a. Add the permissions to the app.** On the app, go to **API permissions →
Add a permission**, choose **Microsoft Graph** (or **SharePoint**), then
**Delegated** or **Application permissions**, search for each name, tick it,
and click **Add permissions**.

| API             | Permission          | Type        | Admin consent required |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------------|------------------------|
| Microsoft Graph | Sites.ReadWrite.All | Delegated   | No                     |
| Microsoft Graph | Sites.Selected      | Delegated   | No                     |
| Microsoft Graph | Sites.Selected      | Application | Yes                    |
| Microsoft Graph | User.Read           | Delegated   | No (added by default)  |
| SharePoint      | Sites.Selected      | Application | Yes                    |

The first one is spelled `Sites.ReadWrite.All`, with no dot between Read and
Write. The two Application rows will show "Not granted for Government of
Ontario" until IT approves them.

**2b. Submit a service desk ticket.** Adding the permissions doesn't by itself
get them approved; the Azure team has to enable them on the backend.

1. Open a ticket with the ITS Service Desk (*Report Issue* on the OPS
   intranet).
2. Ask for the ticket to be routed to **ITS > Service Modernization > GoCloud
   RESPONSE AZURE**.
3. Include the app's **Display name** and **Application (client) ID**, both on
   the app's **Overview** page.
4. Ask them to grant the **Sites.Selected** permissions for **SharePoint** and
   **Microsoft Graph**.

Expect questions, and don't assume the reviewer knows R. Ours told us they
*normally do not grant Application-type permissions* and asked why we needed
both delegated and application access for Graph. What to tell them:

- **Delegated** permissions let R act as you, while you're signed in, limited
  to what you can already see in SharePoint.
- **Application** permissions are for scheduled scripts that run without
  anyone signed in. Sites.Selected is the least-privilege version: it reaches
  only sites an admin explicitly names.

Approval can take a week and a half (ours took about three days).

**Approval is not the end.** Permissions say *what* the app may do; they don't
make sign-in work. You still need Step 3.

## Step 3: Set up sign-in (Authentication)

A new registration has no redirect URI, so sign-in fails with
**AADSTS500113: No reply address is registered**. As the owner, you can fix
this yourself:

1. On the app, open **Authentication** and click **Add Redirect URI**.
2. Choose the platform **Mobile and desktop applications** (Windows, UWP,
   Console…).
3. Leave the suggested URIs unticked and enter this custom redirect URI, then
   click **Configure**:

    ```
    http://localhost:1410
    ```

4. On the **Settings** tab, set **Allow public client flows** to **Yes** and
   save. This allows device-code sign-in, the fallback if the browser redirect
   is ever blocked.

Changes can take a minute or two to take effect.

## Step 4: Set up R

**Install the packages** (once):

```{r}
install.packages(c("AzureGraph", "Microsoft365R"))
```

"Package was built under R version 4.x.x" warnings are harmless.

**Store your IDs in `.Renviron`** so they never appear in scripts. With
sharepointless installed, one line does it (and sets them for the current
session too):

```{r}
sharepointless::less_details_to_renviron(
  tenant = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",  # Directory (tenant) ID
  app    = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"   # Application (client) ID
)
```

Or by hand:

1. In the RStudio console, run `usethis::edit_r_environ()`. The file opens as a
   **tab in the editor pane**. Type into that tab, not the console. Typed into
   the console, these lines fail with "unexpected symbol".
2. Add these two lines, using the IDs from Step 1. Paste the raw value only: no
   quotes, no angle brackets, no spaces around `=`.

    ```
    CLIMICROSOFT365_TENANT=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
    CLIMICROSOFT365_AADAPPID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
    ```

3. Press **Enter** after the last line (R can skip a final line with no
   newline), save with **Ctrl+S**, then **Session → Restart R**.
4. Check that R sees both values:

    ```{r}
    sharepointless::less_details()
    ```

Both should print as 36-character IDs. If either is blank, the file wasn't
saved or R wasn't restarted.

## Step 5: Sign in and connect

### With sharepointless

```{r}
library(sharepointless)

# Paste a library's address straight from the browser...
drive <- less_drive("https://ontariogov.sharepoint.com/sites/<YourSite>/Shared%20Documents/Forms/AllItems.aspx")

# ...or a site address plus part of the library's name
drive <- less_drive("https://ontariogov.sharepoint.com/sites/<YourSite>", library = "^Rapports")

drive$list_files()
```

The first call opens a browser for sign-in (if R asks to create a directory for
saved credentials, answer **Y**). After that, the saved sign-in is reused,
including by scheduled scripts.

### By hand, with AzureGraph and Microsoft365R

**First time only:** create a cached login against *your* app. Passing `app =`
is essential; without it, AzureGraph uses a built-in default app that can see
sites but not their libraries.

```{r}
library(AzureGraph)
library(Microsoft365R)
library(tidyverse)

gr <- create_graph_login(
  Sys.getenv("CLIMICROSOFT365_TENANT"),
  app = Sys.getenv("CLIMICROSOFT365_AADAPPID")
)
```

- If R asks to create a directory for saved credentials, answer **Y**. That
  cache is what lets later sessions skip the browser.
- A browser tab opens for OPS sign-in. Close it when it says authentication is
  complete.
- Confirm the login carries the right permissions. The output must include
  `Sites.ReadWrite.All`:

```{r}
gr$token$credentials$scope
```

**Every session after that:**

```{r}
gr <- get_graph_login(
  Sys.getenv("CLIMICROSOFT365_TENANT"),
  app = Sys.getenv("CLIMICROSOFT365_AADAPPID")
)
```

**Connect to a site and library.** Use the *site* URL, not the URL of a library
view. Trim anything from the library name onward (e.g.
`/Forms/AllItems.aspx`).

```{r}
site <- gr$get_sharepoint_site(
  "https://ontariogov.sharepoint.com/sites/<YourSite>"
)

# Library names on the site
site$list_drives() |> map_chr(\(d) d$properties$name)

# Pick one by partial match: avoids retyping curly apostrophes in French names
drive <- site$list_drives() |>
  keep(\(d) str_detect(d$properties$name, "^<start of library name>")) |>
  pluck(1)

drive$list_files() |> as_tibble()
```

If the last line returns your folders, you're done.

## Troubleshooting

Every error we actually hit, in roughly the order you'll meet them:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `library(Microsoft365R)` seems to hang | It's waiting at a hidden console prompt to create the credentials directory | Click in the console, type `Y`, press Enter |
| `Error: unexpected symbol in "CLIMICROSOFT365_TENANT=..."` | `.Renviron` lines typed into the console | Put them in the `.Renviron` editor tab instead (Step 4), or use `less_details_to_renviron()` |
| Browser shows AADSTS900023, tenant `'.onmicrosoft.com'` | Tenant ID is blank: `.Renviron` not loaded, or placeholders left in | Fix the file, save, restart R, check with `less_details()` |
| Browser shows AADSTS500113, no reply address | App has no redirect URI | Step 3 |
| AADSTS50011 | Redirect URI doesn't match | Make sure it's exactly `http://localhost:1410` under Mobile and desktop applications |
| AADSTS7000218 | Public client flows off | Step 3, Settings tab |
| AADSTS65001 or "Need admin approval" | Permissions not consented | Follow up on your service desk ticket (Step 2b) |
| `No Microsoft Graph logins found for tenant` | `get_graph_login()` only *retrieves* a login | Run `create_graph_login()` once first (Step 5), or let `less_login()` do it |
| `list_drives()` returns `character(0)`; `get_drive()` gives HTTP 403 or `argument to 'which' is not logical` | Login was created without `app =`, so it uses the default app, which has no Sites/Files scopes | Create a login with `app =` and check its scopes (Step 5) |
| `get_sharepoint_site()` fails on a URL ending `/Forms/AllItems.aspx` | That's a library view, not a site | Use the site URL only, or use `less_drive()`, which accepts either |

**Two logins for one tenant.** If you created a default-app login by mistake,
`get_graph_login()` will make you choose between them every session, which
breaks scheduled scripts. Check with `list_graph_logins()`, then run
`delete_graph_login(Sys.getenv("CLIMICROSOFT365_TENANT"))`. It takes no `app`
argument; pick the login that isn't yours from the prompt. If it removes both
instead, just rerun `create_graph_login()` with `app =`.

## Notes and gotchas

**Don't rely on Microsoft365R's default scopes.** Called directly,
`Microsoft365R::get_sharepoint_site()` asks for `Group.ReadWrite.All`,
`Directory.Read.All`, `Sites.ReadWrite.All` and `Sites.Manage.All`, more than
this app is approved for. That triggers an approval wall. The
`create_graph_login()` / `gr$get_sharepoint_site()` route in Step 5 (which
sharepointless uses) avoids it.

**Scheduled jobs (Windows Task Scheduler).** A script run by Task Scheduler
under your Windows account reuses your cached login and will usually work. It
stops when Microsoft demands a fresh sign-in: after a password change, a forced
re-authentication policy, or long inactivity. Run the script interactively once
to seed the cache, and log errors to a file so a broken login doesn't go
unnoticed.

**The truly unattended route** is the Application `Sites.Selected` permission,
which signs in as the app rather than you. Approval alone isn't enough. It also
needs:

- a site-level grant on each named site by a SharePoint admin (who handles this
  in the OPS is unconfirmed)
- a certificate (preferred) or client secret on the app registration

We haven't set up the certificate yet.

**Changing folder permissions** (e.g. making a folder read-only after a
deadline) uses Graph's item permissions endpoint via `do_operation()`. Whether
Graph accepts role changes on SharePoint-group grants is untested. If it
doesn't, the fallback is the SharePoint REST API, which would need an
additional SharePoint permission.
